title: Normalized tensor comparison for an algebraic inverse image at independent site sizes
statement: For sites (C,J) and (D,K) essentially small in a coefficient universe u, with independently sized object and morphism universes, let F be a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint between their sheaves of u-small sets. Let R and RI be commutative ring sheaves and I the specified algebraic inverse-image lift [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] of F from R to RI. For the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there is a natural family I(M tensor_R N) isomorphic to I(M) tensor_RI I(N). For every test sheaf Z and generalized sections x,y,z with z equal to the pure tensor of x,y, the isomorphism sends the transported z to the pure tensor of the transported x,y. This asserts only the algebraic inverse-image comparison, without change of coefficients or scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third Hom/Bilin equality and its proof.

proof.text: Reuse the existing generic geometric module construction and linear-map transport helpers, whose site object and morphism universes are independent. The auxiliary right-module construction specializes their operation comparisons to the adjunction-transposed structural ring map.

Construct the RI-module direct image along the right adjoint using its product comparisons and the adjoint coefficient map R to F_*(RI). Its underlying sheaf is the specified direct image. Its addition and scalar action are the transported operations. The adjunction restricts to a natural bijection of linear maps because the graph equations of I preserve addition and scalar action on universal pairs and triples.

Apply the same transposition to balanced bilinear maps. Test additivity on the two universal triples M times M times N and M times N times N, and balancing on R times M times N. Product preservation and the graph equations make transposition preserve and reflect each equation. Its inverse identities are those of the underlying set-sheaf adjunction.

Use the sheaf tensor universal property on both sides of the bilinear-map bijection. The resulting natural Hom bijection gives mutually inverse linear maps between I(M tensor N) and I(M) tensor I(N). Naturality in M and N follows from transposition. Evaluate at the universal pure pairing, and then precompose any test pair, to obtain the displayed generalized pure-tensor identity. The argument uses no points, nonzero-ring assumption, or equality of the site universes.

proof_origin.note: B9: fully implemented. Transport balanced pairings through the specified set adjunction and graph equations; the tensor universal property proves the comparison invertible. All five universes remain independent.

theorem exists_inverseImageTensorComparison
    (uPush : Sheaf K (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u))
    (adj : uInv ⊣ uPush) [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv] :
    ∃ e : ∀ M N : SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡 R),
        I.modules.obj ((monoidalCategory R).tensorObj M N) ≅
          (monoidalCategory RI).tensorObj (I.modules.obj M) (I.modules.obj N),
      (∀ {M M' N N' : SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡 R)} (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
        I.modules.map ((monoidalCategory R).tensorHom f g) ≫ (e M' N').hom =
          (e M N).hom ≫ (monoidalCategory RI).tensorHom (I.modules.map f) (I.modules.map g)) ∧
      ∀ (M N : SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡 R)) (Z : Sheaf J (Type u))
        (x : Z ⟶ (𝓤 R).obj M) (y : Z ⟶ (𝓤 R).obj N)
        (z : Z ⟶ (𝓤 R).obj ((monoidalCategory R).tensorObj M N)),
        (∀ W t, z.hom.app W t = (tensorObjIsoSheafification M N).inv.val.app W
          (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
            (𝟙 ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R).obj)).unit.app
              (M.val ⊗ N.val)).app W
                ((x.hom.app W t) ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj W] (y.hom.app W t)))) →
        ∀ W t, (e M N).hom.val.app W
          ((uInv.map z ≫ I.moduleUnderlying.inv.app
            ((monoidalCategory R).tensorObj M N)).hom.app W t) =
          (tensorObjIsoSheafification (I.modules.obj M)
            (I.modules.obj N)).inv.val.app W
          (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
            (𝟙 ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj RI).obj)).unit.app
              ((I.modules.obj M).val ⊗ (I.modules.obj N).val)).app W
                (((uInv.map x ≫ I.moduleUnderlying.inv.app M).hom.app W t)
                  ⊗ₜ[RI.obj.obj W]
                  ((uInv.map y ≫ I.moduleUnderlying.inv.app N).hom.app W t)))
